contracts.evidence: 2026-11-15 macOS arm64 (rustc 1.98.0). Oracle: the Go sources at 57c26c76e read statically (internal/daemon/server.go serveConn/handleLine, client.go requestOnce; tests TestOperationTimeoutKeepsConnectionUsable, TestClientReadTimeoutOperationTimeout) plus the sealed capture crates/symbrowse-daemon/tests/fixtures/daemon_oracle/go_timeout.json (already replayed byte-for-byte by lifecycle.rs); Go is not run. Go semantics pinned: the read deadline is re-armed before every frame and covers the whole frame, expiry closes the connection with no response; the operation deadline answers operation_timeout 'daemon operation exceeded its timeout' and the connection stays usable; the handler is never waited for; a vanished client is only noticed on the response write. New process-level tests over a real Unix socket, crates/symbrowse-daemon/tests/deadlines.rs: 12 passed, 0 failed (idle close, deadline re-armed per frame on a reused connection, one-byte-per-100ms trickled frame cut at the read deadline, frame split inside the deadline served, read deadline does not cut a running operation, handler deaf to cancellation answered at the operation deadline with the same and a second connection still served and no second frame on late completion, cooperative handler sees is_cancelled at the deadline, 40 abandoned operations (more than the 32 workers) recover and all 40 handlers see cancellation, pipelined disconnect dispatches exactly once, shutdown cancels a blocked handler and a deaf 10 s handler without waiting, response envelope shape). Existing coverage kept: client timeout code/hint/details and no autostart retry (cancellation.rs, client_contract.rs), late completion emits no second response, production runtime cancellation and same-process restart. Fix: server read_limited_line had only the per-read socket timeout, so a peer trickling one byte per interval held a connection worker forever; it now enforces the absolute per-frame deadline of Go's SetReadDeadline (connection.rs). Rust extension kept: shutdown sets the OperationContext cancelled flag (Go's Close lets handlers finish). Commands: cargo test -p symbrowse-daemon --locked --test deadlines (12/12); cargo test --workspace --locked 452 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored child fixtures. One synthetic corpus of 15 credential vectors (URL userinfo password; URL query token and api_key; argv password=... assignment; argv URL with password; CDP endpoint password via env and via config.toml; secret and adjacent secret line in a syntactically broken config.toml; invalid encryption key; valid 64-hex encryption key; proxy URL password in HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY; MCP method name, tool name and tool argument) is driven through the real symbrowse binary: 16 process runs covering CLI parse errors, read/open/goto and --json against an autostarted static-engine daemon, journal tail, config show (env, TOML, broken TOML, typed TOML), daemon startup with a bad key, `symbrowse mcp --tools all` over stdio with 9 JSON-RPC requests (open/read/fetch_url/fetch_batch/fill errors, unknown tool, unknown method) and daemon stop. Every captured stdout/stderr and every regular file under the isolated HOME/XDG roots (journal, daemon.log, cache, state) is scanned for each secret byte sequence; crates/symbrowse-cli/tests/secret_redaction.rs, 2 passed (the second plants each secret in stdout, stderr and a file to prove the scanner sees all 15). Run against the unfixed tree the corpus test fails, so it is not vacuous. Leaks found and fixed at the root: (1) the action journal wrote URL userinfo passwords and ?token=/&api_key= values verbatim (url_before, url_after, args strings) -> journal.rs scrubs them; (2) config show printed the CDP endpoint userinfo password from env and TOML -> masked in show_fields; (3) TOML parse errors quoted the offending source lines and rejected values -> one-line 'TOML parse error at line L, column C: <class>' without source or value; (4) CLI errors echoed argv (unknown command "password=...", URLs with passwords) -> main.rs scrubs stderr and the stdout of failed runs with the new narrow symbrowse_core::secret_text::scrub (URL userinfo and secret-named name=value pairs only, so 'auth login: ...' and 'unknown flag: --token' stay intact); (5) MCP 'Unknown tool' / 'Method not found' echoed the name -> redact_str; (6) fetch_batch failed items echoed the target URL -> scrubbed.
